prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t point to a single indisputable “best” roofer for hail repair in Denver, but I can help you find the best one for your situation. Here’s a practical way to identify and vet top hail‑damage roofers in Denver, plus red flags to avoid.

How to find the best roofer for hail damage
- Get at least 3 written estimates from local companies experienced with hail claims. Compare scope, materials, labor, warranties, and whether they handle permits/cleanup.
- Look for insurers’ and manufacturers’ credentials: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, or similar manufacturer certifications; Good standing with the BBB.
- Prefer local companies with Denver area references and a physical address (not just a PO box). Local knowledge matters for weather, permitting, and storm patterns.
- Choose contractors experienced with insurance claims and Xactimate estimates. They should be willing to work with your adjuster and explain coverage items.
- Verify licensing and insurance: ask for proof of general liability and workers’ comp insurance. Colorado doesn’t have a single statewide roofing license—confirm any required local registrations/permits.
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer shingle warranty and a workmanship warranty (get it in writing and confirm how long it lasts and whether it’s transferable).
- Check reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi, Nextdoor and the BBB; call recent customers for references if you can.

Important questions to ask every roofer
- How long have you been doing hail-damage work in Denver?
- Are you fully insured (GL and workers’ comp)? Can I see certificates?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand you recommend?
- Will you provide a written estimate and scope of work? Will you handle permits?
- How do you handle insurance claims and supplement requests?
- What is your warranty (workmanship and materials)?
- What is the payment schedule? (Avoid large upfront payments; don’t pay in full until work is completed.)
- Will you provide lien waivers and final cleanup?

Red flags / things to avoid
- Storm-chaser contractors who knock the same day and pressure you to sign.
- Only a cell phone with no local address or no written contract.
- Requests for full payment up front.
- No proof of insurance or evasive answers about licensing/warranty.
- Pressure to accept a payment directly from the contractor rather than through your insurance or to sign over insurance checks without clear documentation.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short vetted checklist/email you can send to 3 contractors.
- Help draft questions for your insurance adjuster.
- Look up top-rated local roofers for your ZIP code (tell me your ZIP and I’ll compile likely candidates and what to check on each).

Which would you like to do next?
